subject: Chemistry
question: Heating 5.00 g of hydrated copper(II) sulfate, CuSO₄·5H₂O (M = 249.7 g mol⁻¹), leaves anhydrous CuSO₄ (M = 159.6 g mol⁻¹). Calculate the theoretical mass of CuSO₄ and the percentage yield if 3.00 g is obtained.
response_text:
CuSO₄·5H₂O(s) → CuSO₄(s) + 5H₂O(g)

n(CuSO₄·5H₂O) = 5.00 / 249.7 = 0.0200 mol
Theoretical mass of CuSO₄ = 0.0200 × 159.6 = 3.19 g
Percentage yield = actual / theoretical × 100 = 3.00 / 3.19 × 100 = 94.0 %

The yield is below 100 % because some solid was lost from the crucible during heating.
